subject: Post-call: Peak moment flowplaybook — QPS, tokens/sec & concurrency checkpoints
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@velotech.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Peak moment flowplaybook — QPS, tokens/sec & concurrency checkpoints

Alex — great call earlier, thanks for walking through the production flow. Quick recap + a small ask so we can finalize a sizing estimate and MAP (mutual action plan).

Highlights I captured from the call:
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline across region with short "peak moments" tied to nightly batch jobs + customer checkout spikes.
- Streaming vs synchronous: routing is a mix — ~65% short sync requests (single-shot completions), ~35% streaming (progressive responses for long-form summarization).
- Current observability: you can export a CSV with per-request token counts; you mentioned a recent 7-day sample that we can use (attach if possible).

Specific items we need to finalize sizing: (please paste numbers or attach a sample CSV)
1) Typical tokens/request (median and p95) and tokens produced by model vs tokens consumed by prompt.
2) Steady-state QPS (avg over business hours) and highest observed 60s-window QPS in last 30 days.
3) Character of the spikes: how long do peak moments last (seconds/minutes)? Any multi-minute sustained windows?
4) Concurrency for streaming: how many simultaneous open streams during peaks?
5) Latency SLO targets — for both sync and streaming tail (e.g., P95, P99 in ms).

What we'll deliver once we have the snapshot:
- A short capacity sketch (GPU pool equivalent, baseline vs reserved vs burst plans).
- Recommended concurrency and batching profiles to meet target latency while minimizing token cost.
- Actionable MAP with milestones: pilot config, loadtest window, production rollout.

I've attached a small template CSV and a sample Redwood sizing estimate (draft) — feel free to replace with your raw export. Can you send the 7-day sample export? If easier, a follow-up 30-min sync tomorrow would also work.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: velotech_workload_snapshot.csv (stub), redwood_sizing_estimate_v1.pdf (stub)

From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@velotech.io>

Cc: Velotech SRE <sre@velotech.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Peak moment flowplaybook — QPS, tokens/sec & concurrency checkpoints

Diego / Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Attached is the 7-day sample export (CSV) and a short note from our SRE with observed windows. High-level numbers below in case the attachment is filtered: 

- Median tokens/request (consumer prompt + model output): 380 tokens
- P95 tokens/request: 1,150 tokens
- Business-hours steady-state QPS: 115 QPS (rolling 1h average)
- Highest observed 60s-window in last 30 days: 2,760 QPS (single 60s spike correlated with scheduled batch)
- Typical peak duration: 20–45 seconds for the short spikes; we see multi-minute (3–8 minutes) spikes roughly 2–3x/day tied to bulk customer imports.
- Concurrent open streaming sessions during peak windows: approx 210 concurrent streams (p95), with median concurrent streaming at 45.
- Latency expectations from product: P95 < 450ms for sync under baseline; P99 < 900ms acceptable for peak windows. For streaming customers prefer sub-1s incremental chunk delivery.

We also noted token mix: ~60% of tokens are model output (assistant), 40% prompt + metadata. If you need any other columns from the export (request id, timestamp, input/output token split) let me know and I can re-export.

—Alex
Alex Romero
Staff SRE, Velotech

Attachment: velotech_7day_export.csv (stub)

Subject: Re: Post-call: Peak moment flowplaybook — QPS, tokens/sec & concurrency checkpoints

Thanks Alex — helpful numbers. Quick internal note and proposed sizing assumptions so Diego can share an update with Velotech: 

Assumptions we’ll use for draft sizing (conservative -> safety margin):
- Request token profile: median 380, p95 1,150 (use provided distribution).
- Effective tokens/sec processing rate per vGPU (baseline compute profile): assume 9,000 tokens/sec for 4-bit quantized LLM variant (batch-friendly).
- Steady-state demand: 115 QPS * median 380 tokens = ~43.7k tokens/sec total load.
- Peak 60s spike: 2,760 QPS * p95 1,150 tokens = ~3,174,000 tokens in that 60s = ~52.9k tokens/sec sustained over 60s (note: check math — we'll reconcile with raw CSV).
- Streaming concurrency: 210 concurrent streams (p95) — streaming keeps KV cache open; we allocate additional capacity per open stream (estimated 1.1x overhead).

Preliminary capacity sketch (reserved + burst):
- Baseline cluster (serve steady-state comfortably): reserve capacity to handle 1.5x steady-state (~65k tokens/sec).
- Burst buffer: autoscale headroom to cover 60s spikes up to 60–80k tokens/sec without quality degradation.
- Concurrency knobs: set streaming connection limit at 300 for the pool, with per-connection rate limiting to avoid tail latency amplification.

Latency targets we can aim for (tight but realistic):
- Sync P95: <= 350ms for typical 512-token responses on reserved pool; P99 <= 700ms on baseline. For peak windows we expect P95 to slip and will rely on burst capacity.
- Streaming: incremental chunk P95 <= 500ms under baseline.

Open asks we still need from Velotech to finalize an estimate:
1) Clarify the time-of-day distribution for the multi-minute spikes (are they concentrated in a daily maintenance window?).
2) Can Velotech tolerate automated fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical customers during extreme peaks?
3) Any regulatory constraints on cold-start (warmup) behavior for on-prem vs hosted?

Next steps: Diego — I can convert this into the sizing sheet and an action plan (pilot loadtest, success criteria, dates). Suggest we propose a 2-hour pilot loadtest window next week and include an initial A/B for a quantized variant.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@velotech.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Peak moment flowplaybook — QPS, tokens/sec & concurrency checkpoints

Diego / Marissa — thanks, that all looks sensible. A couple quick confirmations from our side:
- The multi-minute spikes are mostly during our daily import window at 03:00 UTC and one regional batch at 16:00 UTC — duration closer to 4–7 minutes typically.
- We can tolerate fallback to the quantized variant for 40% of background jobs but want explicit SLA carve-outs for customer-facing flows.
- No special cold-start restrictions for hosted inference; we do want warmup guidance for Private deployments.

Request: please send the updated sizing sheet and the MAP with the pilot window options. Our engineering manager is available Tuesday and Thursday next week for the 2-hour pilot. Once we review the estimate we'll schedule the pilot.

I'll also attach a short excerpt from our exporter (filtered) if that helps. Thanks again — Alex
